issues.title: CPwL-to-network loss transfer lacks hypotheses used in its proof

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $\hat u$ is continuous and piecewise affine on the finite partition $\mathcal T$, we have $\|\nabla \hat u\|_{L^1(\Omega_T)}<\infty$.

issues.failure_explanation: Boundary traces, normals, and the divergence theorem used on K∩Omega_s are not justified for arbitrary measurable sets. Separately, the proof term epsilon times the L1 gradient norm is declared O(epsilon) with a constant independent of h, although the old statement only guarantees that this norm is finite for each CPwL function and permits it to grow with h.
issues.overall_effect: The standalone transfer lemma is not proved at its advertised generality. The particular competitors used later have regular geometric singular sets and locally evident uniform gradient bounds, so those applications can be retained after explicitly checking the restricted hypotheses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Interpret the bound on ∂Ω_s as a uniform finite-perimeter or Lipschitz-boundary hypothesis so that Gauss–Green and boundary traces apply to K∩Ω_s. In the proof, choose the network approximation tolerance of order h²/(1+‖∇û‖_{L¹}) rather than a fixed multiple of h²; Proposition represent permits this without increasing depth or width. This restores h-uniform constants while leaving the lemma and its applications unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The proof uses genuine unstated geometric regularity and an invalid uniformity step, so this is not a typo. Both defects admit short, routine, local corrections supported by the old approximation proposition, with no new construction, rate change, or loss in the intended applications.

issues.title: Shock-birth pieces omitted from the exhaustive decomposition list

failure_location.quote: Each piece is one of the following types: a smooth piece, a regular shock piece, a rarefaction/compound-wave piece, or a shock-shock interaction piece.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \item[(iv)] \emph{Nondegenerate shock-birth pieces and uniform regularity away from birth.}

issues.failure_explanation: Under the literal exhaustive list, no decomposition piece may be a shock-birth piece. This conflicts with item (iv), which specifies precisely such pieces, and makes the simultaneous hypotheses of the intended smooth-initial-data shock-formation theorem empty.
issues.overall_effect: The old assumption does not formally admit the shock-birth regime that the paper separately defines and claims to analyze.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert “or a nondegenerate shock-birth piece” in the exhaustive list of permissible decomposition pieces in Assumption assump:piecewise_smooth.
issues.why_classification: Item (iv) explicitly defines shock-birth pieces, and the smooth-initial-data theorem and its proof explicitly use them. The old source therefore uniquely forces this missing list entry, after which the reader can continue without changing any inference or construction.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Each piece is one of the following types: a smooth piece, a regular shock piece, a rarefaction/compound-wave piece, a shock-shock interaction piece, or a nondegenerate shock-birth piece.

issues.title: Shock-transition cells omitted from the entropy-residual partition

failure_location.quote:
If $K \notin \Lambda_{\Gamma}$, then $u$ is smooth on $K$ and $\hat{u}$ is 
its linear interpolant.

issues.failure_explanation: A strip-only cell belongs to the old complement of Lambda_Gamma, but part of the rapidly varying transition layer lies in it. Therefore eq:away_shock cannot be justified there by the smooth interpolation estimate. The mesh-skeleton condition bounds the aggregate size of these configurations but does not make them absent; that bound still had to be applied.
issues.overall_effect: The O(h) entropy-loss estimate for the single-shock competitor has an unestimated class of cells, and the shock-based results relying on that competitor are incomplete.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define Λ_Γ to contain every background cell meeting the full transition strip, not only cells meeting the exact shock. Treat strip-only cells as a separate local case: their transition-layer contribution is bounded in absolute value, and condition eq:condition_Gamma makes the aggregate contribution O(h). The complement then consists only of cells where û is the smooth interpolant, so the existing competitor and downstream rates remain valid.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine omitted-case error rather than a transcription error. The strip width and the existing mesh-skeleton measure condition directly provide the missing O(h) estimate, so only a short local case estimate is needed and every listed result retains the same statement and rate.

issues.title: Comparison-space bound need not contain the solution approximant
issues.failure_explanation: The stability estimate may use only tests in V_h^c. The chosen test approximates u, yet the old source imposes no relation between c and the range of u. For c below the solution amplitude, the claimed test is outside V_h^c, so substituting it into the minimizer bound is invalid. The same problem recurs for the other solution-adapted comparison functions.
issues.overall_effect: The principal comparison test used to convert small loss into an L1 error estimate is not necessarily admissible, leaving the convergence proofs unsupported for the old unrestricted choice of c.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix c, independently of h, with enough margin that every solution-adapted comparison function satisfies ‖ũ_h‖_{W_h^{1,∞}}≤c. The maximum principle supplies the amplitude bound from ‖u_0‖_{L∞}, while the stated piecewise regularity and the h-scaled interpolation bounds control the gradient part for sufficiently small h. State this choice once and verify it for each comparison construction.
issues.why_classification: The assertion “by construction” omits a real admissibility premise, so it is not a typo. Choosing the test bound above the known solution scale is a routine technical qualification that preserves the method, PDE class, conclusions, rates, and all listed comparison arguments.

issues.title: Negative entropy loss invalidates componentwise loss control
issues.failure_explanation: The old proof claims that the total loss dominates its regularization and initial-data components. This requires the remaining entropy component to be nonnegative, but the old definition is a bare supremum and the raw network output need not lie within the bounded test range. Consequently the strip-selection residual bound and the later initial-trace bound for the minimizer do not follow.
issues.overall_effect: The stability arguments cannot extract residual and initial-trace estimates from the minimizer's small total loss, so the listed convergence theorems are not established by the old proofs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the entropy component by including a zero baseline, namely L_ent(v)=max{0, sup_{k_h∈V_h^c}J_ent(v;k_h)}. Then J_ent(v;k_h)≤L_ent(v) for every test and every loss component is nonnegative. The existing competitor and transfer estimates pass to the positive part, so the residual and initial-trace bounds and all listed convergence rates follow for minimizers of the corrected loss.
issues.why_classification: The bare entropy term can genuinely be negative, and bookkeeping cannot recover componentwise control for minimizers of the original objective. Adding the zero baseline is a contained complete repair with no rate, domain, or complexity loss, but it changes the defining optimization functional and hence gives a comparable corrected algorithm rather than the old algorithmic contract. That makes the issue moderate rather than minor, while no global reconstruction or major mathematical loss is required.

issues.title: Lateral-boundary flux omitted from the stability identity
issues.failure_explanation: The old proof claims that only the final, initial, and artificial jump-interface contributions remain after pairwise interior-face cancellation. In fact, the divergence theorem also yields an integral over the lateral boundary involving the network flux. The assumption that the exact solution is compactly supported does not force a competing network to vanish there, and the old loss contains no term capable of bounding this integral.
issues.overall_effect: The old final-time stability estimates omit an uncontrolled flux term, affecting every convergence proof that uses the same cell-face cancellation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a nonnegative lateral-boundary flux or trace-mismatch penalty to the loss, using the prescribed trace g=0 in the compact-support setting. Retain the lateral face integral in every stability identity and bound it by this penalty. The constructed competitors have the prescribed boundary trace, and the CPwL-to-network transfer acquires only the corresponding routine boundary estimate, so all listed rates and network-size bounds remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Compact support of the exact solution does not control boundary inflow from an arbitrary competing network, so the theorem for minimizers of the old boundary-free loss cannot be restored by a mere proof edit. Adding standard boundary enforcement is a contained modification that preserves the convergence guarantees, but it changes the method’s optimization contract; this is a limited, comparable repair and therefore moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.title: Single-layer construction fails for multiple shock branches in one cell

failure_location.quote: If $K\in\Lambda_\Gamma$, let $\Gamma_K:=K\cap\Gamma$. As in Lemma~\ref{lem:Lu_shock}, choose two planes parallel to the tangent plane of $\Gamma_K$

issues.failure_explanation: The background cell has diameter O(h), while distinct branches outside the O(h^2) interaction tube are only guaranteed to be separated by a constant times h^2. Several branches may therefore lie in one cell. Their union has no single tangent plane, one layer cannot represent all jumps, and the old per-cell prescription does not establish compatible affine traces on common cell faces.
issues.overall_effect: The multidimensional CPwL competitor and its asserted global continuity are not constructed for all geometries permitted by the stated transversality assumption, so the interaction results relying on it are unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each cell outside the interaction patch, decompose K∩Γ into its finitely many connected shock branches. Using their c_sep h² separation, choose thinner disjoint branchwise transition layers and build one common conforming simplicial refinement from globally compatible piecewise-planar offsets, assigning identical vertices and trace values on shared cell faces. Sum the single-branch entropy estimates over the uniformly bounded number of layers and verify that continuity, O(h) loss, and O(h^{-(d+1)}) complexity are retained throughout the affected chain.
issues.why_classification: Repairing the defect requires a genuine multi-interface geometric construction and a compatibility argument, not just changing a symbol or adding a routine estimate. The work remains localized to the multidimensional competitor lemma, uses the existing transversality assumption, and preserves the same loss, rate, complexity, and dependent conclusions, so it is moderate rather than serious.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: \(K\cap\Gamma\) may contain several connected smooth pieces. Let \(\Gamma_K^{(j)}\) denote these smooth pieces.
